```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,

  fig.width = 7,

)

source("R/process_air_quality.R")

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Purpose and data

This project processes air quality measurements from the EPA monitor
at RDU airport and explores patterns in CO, PM2.5, and ozone.
The data cover 2018, 2019, and January-April 2020.
This analysis describes pollution patterns; it does not estimate
associations with sickle cell disease outcomes.

## Data processing

Exact duplicate rows were removed before replacing negative
measurements with zero and calculating daily averages.
This order prevents duplicate records from receiving extra weight
and avoids averaging negative measurement errors with valid values.
Missing values were retained, and absent dates within each file's
observed period were added with missing concentrations.

```{r process-data}
aq_2018 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2018.csv")
aq_2019 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2019.csv")
aq_2020 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2020.csv")

aq_all <- bind_rows(aq_2018, aq_2019, aq_2020) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(aq_all) == 851,
  !anyDuplicated(aq_all$date),
  all(aq_all$CO >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(aq_all$PM25 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(aq_all$O3 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

write.csv(
  aq_all,
  "output/daily_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = ""
)
```

The processed dataset contains `r nrow(aq_all)` calendar days,
with one row per date. CO and ozone are expressed in ppm,
and PM2.5 is expressed in micrograms per cubic meter.

## Annual concentration ranges

These tables show minima and maxima of the cleaned daily
concentrations, excluding missing measurements.
The 2020 table covers January-April only.

```{r annual-ranges, results='asis'}
annual_ranges <- aq_all |>
  select(year, CO, PM25, O3) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CO, PM25, O3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) |>
  group_by(year, pollutant) |>
  summarise(
    minimum = min(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pollutant = factor(
      pollutant,
      levels = c("CO", "PM25", "O3"),
      labels = c(
        "CO (ppm)",
        "PM2.5 (ug/m3)",
        "O3 (ppm)"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(year, pollutant)

for (y in 2018:2020) {

  tab <- annual_ranges |>
    filter(year == y) |>
    transmute(
      Pollutant = pollutant,
      Minimum = sprintf("%.3f", minimum),
      Maximum = sprintf("%.3f", maximum)
    )

  cat("\n\n")

  print(
    knitr::kable(
      tab,
      caption = paste(y, "daily concentration ranges"),
      align = c("l", "r", "r")
    )
  )

  cat("\n\n")
}

write.csv(
  annual_ranges,
  "output/annual_ranges.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Monthly CO and ozone

Daily values for each calendar month were pooled across the
available years. Each confidence interval was calculated as
the mean plus or minus 1.96 times the standard error.
The sample size counts non-missing daily concentrations separately
for each pollutant.

```{r monthly-summary}
monthly_summary <- aq_all |>
  select(month, CO, O3) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CO, O3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) |>
  group_by(month, pollutant) |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    mean_concentration = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_concentration = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    se = sd_concentration / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean_concentration - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean_concentration + 1.96 * se,
    panel = factor(
      pollutant,
      levels = c("CO", "O3"),
      labels = c("CO (ppm)", "O3 (ppm)")
    )
  )

write.csv(
  monthly_summary,
  "output/monthly_CO_O3.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r plot-co-ozone, fig.height=5.5}
plot1 <- ggplot(
  monthly_summary,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = mean_concentration,
    color = pollutant
  )
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ panel,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CO" = "#0072B2",
      "O3" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly CO and ozone concentrations",
    subtitle = "Pooled daily means with 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Concentration",
    caption = "Jan-Apr: three years; May-Dec: two years."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(plot1)

ggsave(
  "output/CO_O3_monthly.png",
  plot1,
  width = 7,
  height = 5.5,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

Separate panels with independent y-axis scales make both pollutants'
patterns readable while retaining their original ppm units.
The vertical heights should not be compared directly between panels.

## Monthly PM2.5 by year

```{r pm25-summary}
pm25_summary <- aq_all |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(PM25)),
    mean_PM25 = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year))

write.csv(
  pm25_summary,
  "output/monthly_PM25.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r plot-pm25}
plot2 <- ggplot(
  pm25_summary,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = mean_PM25,
    color = year,
    group = year
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "#0072B2",
      "2019" = "#D55E00",
      "2020" = "#009E73"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations by year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "PM2.5 (ug/m3)",
    color = "Year",
    caption = "2020 data end in April."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(plot2)

ggsave(
  "output/PM25_monthly.png",
  plot2,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

Lines with points show the sequence of monthly means and make
comparisons between years clear without overlapping daily observations.

## Interpretation

CO concentrations are highest in winter, while ozone concentrations
are generally higher in spring and summer.
January-February 2020 PM2.5 monthly means are lower than those in
2018 and 2019, although 2020 has the largest daily PM2.5 maximum
of 31.200 ug/m3.
Interpretation should account for missing observations and the fact
that January-April include three years of data, whereas May-December
include only two.
